provenance.scope: The vector-representation and relative-velocity gates required by the buckets currently authored in Physics/content. This is not the full grades 9-11 Physics registry.
provenance.deliberately_partial: The V3B core system guide warns that building a large registry before proving its consumer risks another schema-only success. The machinery is proven here against real content; bulk authoring of the remaining grades 9-11 gates is production work, not a plan step.
provenance.adapted_from: The 16-point gate contract in reallaksh19/Common PR #383, generalised to a subject-neutral schema. No gate data was copied; these are authored for the content in this repository.
provenance.review_status: Author-created. No independent scientific or pedagogical review has occurred.

gates.title: Magnitude, vector and signed component

canonical_concepts.statement: A magnitude is a nonnegative length; it carries no direction information.
A component is a signed reading along a declared axis; its sign is direction information, not a defect.
The signed component pair and the magnitude are two descriptions of one vector, not two separate quantities.

external_prerequisites.statement: Read and subtract signed coordinates on an axis, preserving the sign.
Obtain the hypotenuse length from two perpendicular leg lengths.

relations.meaning: The magnitude of a vector is the hypotenuse of the right triangle formed by its perpendicular components.

symbols.meaning: Signed component along the declared x axis
Signed component along the declared y axis

conditions: The two axes are perpendicular.
Both components are expressed in the same frame and the same unit.
Squaring removes the component signs, so the magnitude alone cannot recover direction.

required_labels.label: equal coordinate scale on both axes

representations.verification_method: Read the endpoint coordinates off the drawn axes and confirm they reproduce the stated signed components; confirm equal coordinate scale on both axes.
must_not_imply: That arrow length alone communicates the numeric value without a stated scale.
That a vector drawn from a different origin is a different vector.

validity_conditions: A frame with declared positive directions exists before any component is read.
Classical kinematics; no relativistic composition.

reasoning_sequence.action: Declare the frame and the positive direction of each axis.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: A signed component has no meaning without a declared positive direction.

reasoning_sequence.action: Read each component with its sign.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The sign is the axis reading itself, not an adjustment applied afterwards.

reasoning_sequence.action: Apply the right-triangle relation to the component magnitudes.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Perpendicular components are the legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is the vector length.

reasoning_sequence.action: Report the magnitude as nonnegative and retain the signed pair for direction.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Squaring erased the signs, so direction must come from the retained components.

transformations.statement: A vector may be replaced by its signed component pair along declared perpendicular axes, and reconstructed from them.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Stating the magnitude fully answers a question about the vector.
misconceptions.counterexample: (3,4) m/s and (4,3) m/s both have magnitude 5 m/s but point in different directions.
misconceptions.repair: Compute both magnitudes, observe they agree, then compare the signed components directly to see the vectors differ.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A negative component means a negative speed.
misconceptions.counterexample: A velocity of (0,-4) m/s has speed 4 m/s, not -4 m/s.
misconceptions.repair: Separate the signed component, which carries direction, from the magnitude, which is taken nonnegative after squaring.

problem_families.title: Given signed components, state magnitude and direction
hidden_invariants: The magnitude is invariant under reversing both components.

difficulty.note: Few steps, but the component/magnitude distinction is the failure point, not the arithmetic.

falsification_cases.mutation: Remove the declared axis directions from the representation's required labels.
Delete the unit field from a relation symbol.

gates.title: Axis choice is free, but once declared it fixes every sign

canonical_concepts.statement: The positive direction of each axis is a free declaration, not a property of the physical situation.
Once declared, the convention fixes the sign of every component measured along that axis.

relations.expression: reversing a declared positive axis direction negates every component measured along it
relations.meaning: A change of convention changes the numbers describing the vector without changing the vector.

symbols.meaning: Component of the same vector under the reversed convention

conditions: Only the axis whose positive direction was reversed changes sign.
The physical vector is unchanged; only its description changes.

required_labels.label: both axis positive directions named in words
equal coordinate scale on both axes

representations.verification_method: Re-declare one axis in the opposite direction and confirm the magnitude is unchanged while that axis's component changes sign.
must_not_imply: That one convention is physically correct and another is wrong.

validity_conditions: Axes remain perpendicular and non-rotating under the re-declaration.

reasoning_sequence.action: State both positive directions explicitly.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Component signs are only meaningful relative to a stated convention.

reasoning_sequence.action: Re-express the same vector under a reversed convention.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Reversing a declared direction negates components measured along it.

reasoning_sequence.action: Confirm the magnitude is unchanged.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The magnitude relation squares both components, so a single sign flip does not change it.

transformations.statement: A declared axis reversal maps every component along that axis to its negative and leaves the magnitude fixed.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A component should be made positive because the object is moving forward.
misconceptions.counterexample: With east declared positive, an object moving west has a negative x component however natural its motion feels.
misconceptions.repair: Return to the declared axis and read the sign from it; 'forward' is not an axis unless it was declared as one.

problem_families.title: Restate a vector under a different declared convention

falsification_cases.mutation: Add this gate to its own prerequisites.

gates.title: Subtraction as addition of the reversed vector

canonical_concepts.statement: Subtracting a vector is defined as adding its reverse.
A free vector may be translated without rotation for a tail-to-head construction.

relations.meaning: Component-wise, (P-Q)x = Px - Qx and (P-Q)y = Py - Qy; geometrically, reverse Q and add tail-to-head.

symbols.meaning: First vector in the declared frame
Second vector in the same frame
Q reversed: equal magnitude, opposite direction

conditions: P and Q are expressed along the same declared axes.
Reversal preserves magnitude and negates every component.

required_labels.label: labelled P, Q and the resultant

representations.verification_method: Compare the drawn resultant's components against the direct component subtraction; both routes must agree.
must_not_imply: That joining the two arrowheads in an arbitrary order gives the difference.
That reversal changes a vector's length.

validity_conditions: Axes are parallel and non-rotating throughout the construction.
A zero resultant has no assigned direction.

reasoning_sequence.action: Reverse Q.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Negating a vector preserves its length and flips both signed components.

reasoning_sequence.action: Translate the reversed vector to the head of P without rotating it.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: A free vector is defined by length and direction, not by where it is drawn.

reasoning_sequence.action: Draw the resultant from the tail of P to the head of the translated reverse.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Tail-to-head addition gives the vector sum, here P + (-Q).

reasoning_sequence.action: Reconcile against direct component subtraction.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The graphical and component routes compute the same operation and must agree.

transformations.statement: Reversing the operand order negates the result: Q - P = -(P - Q).

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Vector subtraction means joining the two arrowheads in whichever order looks convenient.
misconceptions.counterexample: For P=(6,0) and Q=(0,8) m/s the two tip-joining orders give (6,-8) and (-6,8) m/s, which are opposite vectors.
misconceptions.repair: Perform the explicit reverse-then-add construction; the shortcut hides which order was taken.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Reversing a vector changes its magnitude.
misconceptions.counterexample: (0,8) m/s and (0,-8) m/s both have magnitude 8 m/s.
misconceptions.repair: Apply the magnitude relation to both; squaring the components makes the sign irrelevant to length.

problem_families.title: Construct a vector difference graphically and confirm by components
hidden_invariants: The graphical and component routes must agree.

falsification_cases.mutation: Change the representation kind to one the subject contract does not declare.

gates.title: Position measured from another object at the same instant

canonical_concepts.statement: Relative position compares two positions recorded at the same instant.
Following origin to B to A gives r_A = r_B + r_A/B, from which the subtraction order follows.

relations.meaning: The displacement from B to A, obtained by subtracting same-instant common-origin positions.

symbols.meaning: Position of A in the common frame at the stated instant
Position of B in the same frame at the same instant
Position of A measured from B, with parallel axes

conditions: Both positions are taken at the same instant.
Axes are parallel and non-rotating.
Positions at different instants do not define this quantity.

required_labels.label: the displacement from B to A
equal coordinate scale on both axes

representations.verification_method: Add the drawn relative position to B's position and confirm A's position is recovered.
must_not_imply: That the subtraction order is interchangeable.
That positions taken at different instants may be compared this way.

validity_conditions: Classical kinematics in a common, non-rotating frame.

reasoning_sequence.action: Follow the path origin to B to A.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Vector displacements add along consecutive paths.

reasoning_sequence.action: Subtract r_B from both sides of r_A = r_B + r_A/B.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The same vector operation applied to both sides preserves the equality.

transformations.statement: Swapping the two objects negates the relative position.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Subtract whichever position is written first in the question.
misconceptions.counterexample: With A at (7,2) m and B at (3,5) m, r_A/B is (4,-3) m but r_B/A is (-4,3) m: the two orders point opposite ways.
misconceptions.repair: Reconstruct the path origin to B to A explicitly before subtracting.

problem_families.title: Construct a relative position from two same-instant positions
hidden_invariants: Adding the result back to B recovers A.

falsification_cases.mutation: Empty the counterexample on the subtraction-order misconception.

gates.title: Relative velocity in a plane

canonical_concepts.statement: Relative velocity compares how one simultaneous separation changes over one shared time interval.
For constant velocities the relative velocity is the vector difference of common-frame velocities.

relations.meaning: The velocity of A as measured by an observer moving with B, for parallel non-rotating axes.

symbols.meaning: Velocity of A in the common frame
Velocity of B in the same frame at the same instant
Velocity of A relative to B

conditions: Same observation times and one common interval.
Parallel, non-rotating Cartesian axes.
Classical speeds; relativistic velocity addition does not apply.
A finite-interval average is not automatically an instantaneous velocity when motion varies.

required_labels.label: resultant labelled as the relative velocity

representations.verification_method: Confirm the drawn resultant's components equal the component-wise difference, and that a same-interval position change reproduces it.
must_not_imply: That subtracting speeds gives the relative speed when directions differ.
That a correct magnitude certifies a correct direction.

validity_conditions: Parallel non-rotating axes; a rotating frame requires additional terms not covered by this gate.
Non-relativistic speeds.

reasoning_sequence.action: Write the relative position at two instants.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The relative-position relation applies at each instant separately.

reasoning_sequence.action: Subtract them and group the displacement changes.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Vector subtraction distributes across the two same-instant equations.

reasoning_sequence.action: Divide every term by the same non-zero interval.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Each quotient is an average velocity over that shared interval.

reasoning_sequence.action: For constant velocities, identify each average with the constant velocity.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: No instantaneous limit is required when the velocity does not vary.

transformations.statement: Relative velocities compose: v_A/C = v_A/B + v_B/C, which is why a three-object situation may require addition rather than subtraction.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Subtracting the two speeds always gives the relative speed.
misconceptions.counterexample: A at (6,0) m/s and B at (0,8) m/s have speeds 6 and 8 m/s, yet the relative speed is 10 m/s, not 2 m/s.
misconceptions.repair: Subtract signed components first, then take the magnitude only if a magnitude was asked for.

problem_families.title: Two velocities in a common translating frame
hidden_invariants: Equal velocities give zero relative velocity.
A stationary observer gives v_A/B = v_A.

difficulty.note: The derivation is short but the common-interval justification is the step most often skipped.

falsification_cases.mutation: Make the divide step depend on a later step.
Reuse REL-RELATIVE-VELOCITY as a relation id in another gate.

gates.title: Reversing the observer reverses the relative vector

canonical_concepts.statement: The relative-velocity relation is antisymmetric in its two objects.
Reversal changes direction but not magnitude.

relations.meaning: Swapping which object is the observer negates every component of the relative velocity.

symbols.meaning: Velocity of A relative to B
Velocity of B relative to A

conditions: Both are evaluated in the same frame at the same instant.
The magnitude relation squares components, so the magnitude is unchanged.

required_labels.label: named observer for the drawn vector
vector symbol for each drawn vector
equal coordinate scale on both axes

representations.verification_method: Add the two relative vectors and confirm the sum is exactly zero.
must_not_imply: That a correct length establishes a correct observer order.

validity_conditions: Same conditions as the relative-velocity gate it depends on.

reasoning_sequence.action: Swap the subtraction order.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The relation is defined by that order, so swapping it negates the result.

reasoning_sequence.action: Add the two relative vectors and confirm zero.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: A vector plus its negative is the zero vector.

transformations.statement: v_A/B + v_B/A = 0 for any pair of velocities in a common frame.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A correct length is enough for a correct relative-velocity answer.
misconceptions.counterexample: If v_A/B is (6,-8) m/s pointing southeast, an answer of (6,8) m/s has the same magnitude 10 m/s but points northeast, describing a different observation.
misconceptions.repair: Name the observer, label both signed components, and inspect direction before taking any magnitude.

problem_families.title: Obtain the reversed-observer vector from a known result
hidden_invariants: The two relative vectors sum to zero.

falsification_cases.mutation: Point the prerequisite at a gate id that does not exist.

gates.title: Resolve a magnitude-and-angle vector into perpendicular components

canonical_concepts.statement: Sine/cosine component assignment is determined by which axis the stated angle is measured from: cosine is adjacent and sine is opposite.
Right-triangle ratios give component magnitudes; signed directions come from the declared axes/quadrant.

external_prerequisites.statement: Use sine and cosine ratios in a right triangle to obtain leg magnitudes from a hypotenuse and acute reference angle.

relations.expression: V_adj = V cos(theta); V_opp = V sin(theta)
relations.meaning: Resolve a vector magnitude into component magnitudes adjacent/opposite to an explicitly stated acute reference angle, then assign signs from the declared axes.

symbols.meaning: Acute reference angle to one component axis

conditions: The component axes are perpendicular.
The reference axis for theta is explicitly identified.
Signs are attached from the declared axis directions after the component magnitudes are found.

validity_conditions: Do not assign sine/cosine by x/y labels until the angle reference is identified.
Keep component signs separate from the nonnegative right-triangle leg magnitudes.

reasoning_sequence.action: Identify the axis from which the given acute angle is measured.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Adjacent/opposite roles are defined relative to that angle.

reasoning_sequence.action: Use cosine for the adjacent component magnitude and sine for the opposite magnitude.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: These are the right-triangle projection ratios.

reasoning_sequence.action: Attach signs from the declared positive axes.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Direction is encoded by signed components, not by positive triangle lengths.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: The x-component is always V cos(theta).
misconceptions.counterexample: If theta is measured from +y, the y-component is adjacent and takes the cosine magnitude.
misconceptions.repair: Mark the reference axis first, then label adjacent/opposite before x/y.

problem_families.title: Resolve a magnitude-and-angle vector for later plane-motion use
hidden_invariants: The resolved pair reconstructs the same vector magnitude.
Changing the angle reference description does not change the physical vector.

falsification_cases.mutation: Remove the unit field from one declared relation symbol.

gates.title: Independent perpendicular components under common time

canonical_concepts.statement: In a fixed Cartesian frame, perpendicular motion components evolve independently under their own acceleration components while sharing the same elapsed time.
A two-dimensional velocity or displacement is reconstructed from its signed perpendicular components; solving one component does not erase the other.

relations.expression: v_x = u_x + a_x t; v_y = u_y + a_y t
relations.meaning: For constant acceleration components over one shared interval, each velocity component follows the one-dimensional constant-acceleration relation independently.
conditions: a_x and a_y are constant over the interval.
Both component equations use the same elapsed time and frame.

relations.expression: Delta x = u_x t + 0.5 a_x t^2; Delta y = u_y t + 0.5 a_y t^2
relations.meaning: For constant acceleration components over one shared interval, each displacement component follows the one-dimensional constant-acceleration relation independently.
conditions: a_x and a_y are constant over the interval.
Both component equations use the same elapsed time and frame.

validity_conditions: Use one fixed non-rotating Cartesian frame.
The same time interval applies to x and y components.
Each acceleration component is constant before the constant-acceleration equations are used.

reasoning_sequence.action: Declare one x-y frame and write initial velocity/acceleration as signed components.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Component signs and equations require one common coordinate description.

reasoning_sequence.action: Write separate x and y equations with the same t.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Perpendicular component dynamics evolve independently but describe the same event time.

reasoning_sequence.action: Reconstruct the requested vector magnitude/direction or position from the solved components.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The physical two-dimensional state is the combined component pair.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: The x and y motions may be solved with unrelated elapsed times because they are independent.
misconceptions.counterexample: A projectile's horizontal and vertical coordinates at one physical instant must use the same t.
misconceptions.repair: Independence means separate component equations, not separate clocks.

problem_families.title: Solve plane motion by component constant-acceleration equations
hidden_invariants: One common time couples the component descriptions of the same event.
Each component uses only its own initial velocity and acceleration.

falsification_cases.mutation: Remove the unit field from one declared component-relation symbol.

gates.title: Projectile motion as a special two-dimensional constant-acceleration model

canonical_concepts.statement: In the ideal near-Earth projectile model after release, air resistance is neglected, horizontal acceleration is zero and vertical acceleration is constant downward g.
Horizontal and vertical projectile components share one elapsed time; horizontal launch and oblique launch are initial-condition variations of the same model.

relations.expression: a_x = 0; a_y = -g; v_x = u_x; v_y = u_y - g t; Delta x = u_x t; Delta y = u_y t - 0.5 g t^2
relations.meaning: With +y upward and air resistance neglected near Earth, projectile motion is the 2D constant-acceleration model specialized to zero horizontal acceleration and constant downward gravitational acceleration.

symbols.meaning: Horizontal velocity component at time t
Vertical velocity component at time t

conditions: Near-Earth region with approximately constant g.
Air resistance neglected.
+y is declared upward for the displayed signs.
The object is in free flight after release.

validity_conditions: Do not apply the ideal projectile model while a contact/propulsion force is still acting.
State the vertical sign convention before writing a_y=-g.
Horizontal and oblique launch are handled by changing u_x/u_y, not by changing the physical model.

reasoning_sequence.action: Decide whether the object is in free flight under gravity alone with air resistance neglected.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: That model choice determines whether the projectile component equations are justified.

reasoning_sequence.action: Express the initial velocity as u_x/u_y; resolve a launch angle only if the question supplies one.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Initial conditions determine the component histories while the gravitational acceleration model stays fixed.

reasoning_sequence.action: Solve x and y components with one common time and reconstruct the requested speed/direction/position.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The component equations describe the same projectile at the same instant.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A projectile needs a horizontal force to keep moving horizontally.
misconceptions.counterexample: With air resistance neglected, horizontal velocity remains constant after release because horizontal acceleration is zero.
misconceptions.repair: Separate velocity from acceleration: nonzero v_x does not require nonzero a_x.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Horizontal and vertical projectile motions can use different flight times.
misconceptions.counterexample: The object has one physical position at each instant; both component coordinates correspond to the same t.
misconceptions.repair: Use one shared time variable in both component equations.

problem_families.title: Horizontal and oblique projectile questions from component motion
hidden_invariants: One common time links x and y.
Gravity changes only the vertical velocity in the ideal model.
Range/height/time-of-flight are consequences of the component model, not separate physical laws.

falsification_cases.mutation: Remove the unit field from one projectile-relation symbol.

gates.title: Recover vector direction and normalize a 2-D unit direction

canonical_concepts.statement: The signed component pair and v_x i-hat + v_y j-hat are equivalent descriptions of the same two-dimensional vector.
Component signs determine the quadrant or axis; inverse tangent of positive component magnitudes supplies only an acute reference angle to place inside that direction.
A unit-direction vector is obtained by dividing a nonzero vector by its positive magnitude; the zero vector cannot be normalized because it has no direction and would require division by zero.

external_prerequisites.statement: Use inverse tangent on a positive right-triangle ratio to recover an acute reference angle.

relations.meaning: A two-dimensional vector expressed on declared perpendicular x/y axes can be written equivalently as the signed x coefficient times the +x unit basis vector plus the signed y coefficient times the +y unit basis vector.

symbols.meaning: Dimensionless unit basis vector along declared +x
Dimensionless unit basis vector along declared +y

conditions: The x and y axes are declared and perpendicular.
i_hat and j_hat name the positive unit directions of those axes.
The signed coefficients retain the physical units of the vector components.

relations.expression: alpha = arctan(|v_y|/|v_x|); component signs determine the quadrant
relations.meaning: For a nonzero vector with both perpendicular components nonzero, inverse tangent of the positive component-magnitude ratio gives an acute reference angle; the signed components independently determine the quadrant in which that reference angle must be placed.

symbols.meaning: Acute reference angle to the x-axis

conditions: The vector is nonzero.
When both components are nonzero, use positive component magnitudes for the acute ratio.
If either component is zero, report the exact axis direction directly rather than dividing by zero.
Quadrant selection comes from component signs, not from the inverse-tangent output alone.

relations.meaning: Dividing a nonzero vector and every signed component by the same positive magnitude produces a dimensionless vector of magnitude 1 in the same direction.

symbols.meaning: Unit vector in the direction of v

conditions: Every component is divided by the same magnitude.
The component axes and basis notation refer to the same declared frame.

validity_conditions: Axes are declared and perpendicular before components or basis notation are interpreted.
Direction recovery applies only to a nonzero vector; exact-axis cases are handled directly.
Normalization applies only when |v|>0.
Dot product, scalar projection, cross product, three-dimensional vector algebra and calculus are outside this gate.

reasoning_sequence.action: Translate signed components into i-hat/j-hat notation without changing signs.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The basis symbols name the declared positive axis directions.

reasoning_sequence.action: Use component signs to fix the quadrant or exact axis.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The signs preserve direction information before any ratio is formed.

reasoning_sequence.action: When both components are nonzero, obtain an acute reference angle from the positive component-magnitude ratio.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The component magnitudes are the legs of the right triangle and inverse tangent supplies the acute reference angle.

reasoning_sequence.action: For a nonzero vector, divide every signed component by the same positive magnitude and verify the resulting magnitude is 1.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: A common positive scale factor preserves direction while setting the length to 1.

transformations.statement: (v_x,v_y) and v_x i_hat + v_y j_hat encode the same vector in the same declared axes.
For |v|>0, v -> v/|v| preserves direction and changes magnitude to 1.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: The raw value of tan^-1(v_y/v_x) is always the final direction.
misconceptions.counterexample: A vector with v_x<0 and v_y>0 lies in quadrant II even though the signed ratio is negative; the quadrant must be fixed from the component signs.
misconceptions.repair: Use signs first for quadrant, then use an acute reference angle from positive component magnitudes and place it in that quadrant.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: The zero vector can be normalized in the same way as any other vector.
misconceptions.counterexample: For v=(0,0), |v|=0, so v/|v| would divide by zero and there is no direction to preserve.
misconceptions.repair: Check |v|>0 before normalization; refuse the zero vector.

problem_families.title: Recover a quadrant-correct vector direction from signed components
hidden_invariants: The final direction must reproduce the original component sign pattern.

problem_families.title: Normalize a nonzero 2-D vector to unit direction
hidden_invariants: The normalized vector has magnitude 1 and the same component sign pattern as the original.

difficulty.note: The formulas are short; the hard decisions are preserving quadrant information and respecting the zero-vector boundary.

falsification_cases.mutation: Remove the unit field from one declared relation symbol.
